name: North American Sabreliner
summary: North American business jet designed for the T-39 military trainer program, using a thin swept wing and tail resembling the F-86 Sabre; many ex-military examples remain in private service.

wings: Wing and tail styled after the F-86
engines: Two engines mounted on the rear fuselage with short fairings
Round intakes ahead of each engine pod
fuselage: Sleek, narrow fuselage with a pointed nose and small oval windows
Tapering rear fuselage carrying the engine pods
tail: Swept fin with a conventional low-set tailplane
Distinctive sharp tail sweep reminiscent of the F-86

tellTales: Swept-wing business jet with rear-mounted engines and a conventional (non-T) tail
Thin, sharply swept wing and tail that look like a scaled-up fighter
Small oval windows on a narrow fuselage

confusedWith.howToTell: The Learjet has wingtip tanks and delta fins under the tail; the Sabreliner has a thicker, more swept wing and no tip tanks.
The Hawker has a longer, rounder fuselage with a ventral fin and larger windows; the Sabreliner has a narrow fuselage with small oval windows.
The Citation has a straight wing, T-tail and engines on the rear fuselage; the Sabreliner has a swept wing and a conventional tail.
The T-33 has straight wings with tip tanks; the Sabreliner has swept wings with no tip tanks.
